newsitem.title: USA: FDA does not approve generic Premarin estrogen.
newsitem.headline: FDA does not approve generic Premarin estrogen.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said Monday it would not approve at this time a generic version of Premarin, a widely-used estrogen replacement therapy drug for menopausal women.

The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research said it would not approve a synthetic generic version because the products have not been proven to work the same as the original brand-name drug in treating menopausal symptoms and preventing osteoporosis.

Generic drug makers do not have to repeat all the clinical trials necessary for a new brand-name drug to get approved but they do have to establish that the ingredients are the same and they are absorbed and used by the body in the same way.

Premarin, made by Wyeth-Ayerst, a unit of American Home Products, was approved in 1942. It is the brand name for conjugated estrogens derived from the urine of pregnant mares and it contains a number of different estrogens.
There are other brand-name and generic drugs based on other estrogen therapies.
